item.title: Zodiac
item.description:
David Fincher’s masterpiece of sustained tension deftly shows there’s more than one way to lose your life to a killer. Based on Robert Graysmith’s true crime tome, Zodiac follows a team of police investigators and newspaper reporters as they doggedly chase leads and slowly put together the pieces of the notorious mystery as their yearslong search pushes past the point of personal obsession. A large ensemble cast shines with Jake Gyllenhaal, Mark Ruffalo, and Robert Downey Jr. providing career-best performances. “David Fincher’s grim but mesmerizing Zodiac offers the puzzle-solving addictiveness of a detective story, the shivers of a thriller and the allure of a character study, all presented with a dash of newspaper drama.” – Moira MacDonald, Seattle Times “ Zodiac is the All the President’s Men of serial killer movies, with Woodward and Bernstein played by a cop and a cartoonist. It’s not merely “based” on California’s infamous Zodiac killings, but seems to exude the very stench and provocation of the case.” – Roger Ebert

Durata: 157 minuti

item.title: Ocean’s Eleven (2001)
item.description:
3 casinos. 11 guys. 150 million bucks. Ready to win big? The con is on in Steven Soderbergh’s crackerjack update of the classic Rat Pack caper. Fresh out of the slammer, Danny Ocean assembles a team to orchestrate the most daring heist in Last Vegas history. But this mission might be more than just about money. George Clooney, Matt Damon, Andy Garcia, Brad Pitt, and Julia Roberts headline an all-star cast in the witty, propulsive, and incredibly cool Ocean’s Eleven . “Soderbergh’s crisp, funny heist flick makes out like a bandit. George Clooney and Elliott Gould steal the show.” – Stephanie Zacharek, Salon.com “This wholly enjoyable entertainment sees Soderbergh setting himself a new challenge – the hi-tech robbery procedural – and relishing the clichés even as he freshens them with a dab of polish, wit, pace and a light touch of irony.” – Geoff Andrew, Time Out
Cast: Director: Steven Soderbergh | Writer: Screenplay by Ted Griffin | Starring: George Clooney, Matt Damon, Andy Garcia, Brad Pitt, Julia Roberts, Casey Affleck, Scott Caan, Don Cheadle, Elliott Gould, Bernie Mac, Carl Reiner | Year: 2001 | Country: USA | Format: 35mm
Durata: 116 minuti

item.title: Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood
item.description:
Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age. “The film is Quentin Tarantino’s magnum opus – a sweeping statement on an entire generation of American popular culture and an almost expressionistic rendering of the counterculture forming at its margins, gradually growing in influence.” – Sam C. Mac, Slant Magazine “As a film about making films, and the agony and ecstasy of everything we love about movies, Tarantino knocks it out of the park.” – Hannah Woodhead, Little White Lies “It’s a heady, engrossing, kaleidoscopic, spectacularly detailed nostalgic splatter collage of a film, an epic tale of backlot Hollywood in 1969” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “An absolute blast, a pure, giddy rush of thrillingly confident, expansive filmmaking that showcases the most resonant and satisfying storytelling Tarantino has given us” – Jessica Kiang, Sight & Sound
Cast: Director: Quentin Tarantino | Writer: Quentin Tarantino | Starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt, Margot Robbie, Emile Hirsch, Margaret Qualley, Timothy Olyphant, Austin Butler, Dakota Fanning, Bruce Dern, Al Pacino | Year: 2019 | Country: USA | Format: 35mm
Durata: 161 minuti

Orari: Fri November 27 - 11:59 pm

item.title: Hot Water (Silent with Live Music Score)
item.description:
Featuring live musical accompaniment by Cliff Retallick. Rare 35mm screening! A hilarious domestic-life comedy begins with Harold with an armful of packages and a live turkey on a streetcar, followed by a disastrous spin in his new car with his in-laws, and ending with haunted house-type thrills provoked by his mother-in-law (Josephine Cromwell). plus bonus Harold Lloyd short An Eastern Westerner (1920) at the start of the show! Harold is a spoiled east coast youth packed off to a ranch in the west in this fast and furious parody of western films.

item.title: Batman Returns
item.description:
Tim Burton’s massively entertaining follow-up to his groundbreaking Batman blockbuster goes bigger and bolder with the Penguin (Danny DeVito), Catwoman (Michelle Pfeiffer), and corrupt businessman Max Shrek (Christopher Walken) out to rid the world of the caped crusader (Michael Keaton). Batman Returns remains one of filmdom’s most ambitious sequels, showcasing incredible production design and visual effects, along with standout performances. “ Batman Returns is the rarest of Hollywood beasts – a sequel that’s better than the original” – Jay Carr, Boston Globe “Burton gives the material a luxurious masked-ball quality and a sly contemporary wit” – Terrence Rafferty, New Yorker “Drawing upon the fairy-tale spirit of his more freewheeling fables – Edward Scissorhands , Beetlejuice , Pee-wee’s Big Adventure – Mr. Burton creates a wicked world of misfits, all of them rendered with the mixture of horror, sympathy and playfulness that has become this director’s hallmark.” – Janet Maslin, The New York Times
Cast: Director: Tim Burton | Writer: Screenplay by Daniel Waters, Story by Daniel Waters and Sam Hamm | Starring: Michael Keaton, Danny DeVito, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken, Michael Gough, Pat Hingle, Michael Murphy | Year: 1992 | Country: USA | Format: 35mm
Durata: 126 minuti

item.title: Paper Moon (Special Guests) / Nickelodeon (Special Guest)
item.description:
Just added! Peter Bogdanovich friend & collaborator Colleen Camp will introduce the screening, schedule permitting. Sam Wasson, editor of the new Bogdanovich memoirs What I Really Want to Do is Direct , will join us for a Q&A following the film moderated by Kim Morgan, schedules permitting. In Peter Bogdanovich’s warm & funny period piece, real life father & daughter pair Ryan & Tatum O’Neal star as a bible salesman conman and a precocious tomboy who may or may not be related. As the unlikely duo hit the road, a poignant friendship evolves as they concoct various scams & schemes amidst the backdrop of the Great Depression. Featuring striking black and white cinematography by László Kovács and an Academy Award winning performance for the young O’Neal in her film debut. “Tatum O’Neal makes a sensational screen debut.” – Variety “I wonder how many moviegoers will be prepared for the astonishing confidence and depth that Tatum brings to what’s really the starring role. I’d heard about how good she was supposed to be, but I nevertheless expected a kind of clever cuteness, like we got from Shirley Temple or young Elizabeth Taylor. Not at all. Tatum O’Neal creates a character out of thin air, makes us watch her every moment and literally makes the movie work” – Roger Ebert Just added! Actor Jeffrey Byron will join us IN PERSON, schedule permitting, to introduce the film. Burt Reynolds and Ryan O’Neal star in this heartfelt valentine to the early days of moviemaking. O’Neal is the film director who literally stumbles into his job, and Reynolds is an overnight screen hero. Based on actual reminiscences of such veterans as Raoul Walsh and Allan Dwan. (Sony)
Cast: Director: Peter Bogdanovich | Writer: Screenplay by Alvin Sargent based on the novel "Addie Pray" by Joe David Brown | Starring: Ryan O'Neal, Tatum O'Neal, Madeline Kahn, John Hillerman | Year: 1973 | Country: USA | Format: 35mm | Director: Peter Bogdanovich | Writer: Written by W.D. Richter and Peter Bogdanovich | Starring: Ryan O'Neal, Burt Reynolds, Tatum O'Neal, Brian Keith, Stella Stevens, John Ritter, Jeffrey Byron | Year: 1976 | Country: USA | Format: 35mm
Durata: 121 minuti

item.title: Exorcist II: The Heretic
item.description:
It’s four years later… what does she remember? Can a Vatican investigator (Richard Burton) and a psychiatric specialist (Louise Fletcher) unlock the secrets of Regan’s demonic ordeal? Linda Blair returns in Zardoz director John Boorman’s visually striking, freaked out follow-up to William Friedkin’s horror masterpiece. Filmmaker Martin Scorsese once asserted, “I like the first Exorcist … but The Heretic surpasses it.”

item.title: Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood
item.description:
Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age. “The film is Quentin Tarantino’s magnum opus – a sweeping statement on an entire generation of American popular culture and an almost expressionistic rendering of the counterculture forming at its margins, gradually growing in influence.” – Sam C. Mac, Slant Magazine “As a film about making films, and the agony and ecstasy of everything we love about movies, Tarantino knocks it out of the park.” – Hannah Woodhead, Little White Lies “It’s a heady, engrossing, kaleidoscopic, spectacularly detailed nostalgic splatter collage of a film, an epic tale of backlot Hollywood in 1969” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “An absolute blast, a pure, giddy rush of thrillingly confident, expansive filmmaking that showcases the most resonant and satisfying storytelling Tarantino has given us” – Jessica Kiang, Sight & Sound
